Stav is Lost: 11.9 mi out/back from Maroon Lake, 'Net Gain 5,200 ft'; cites no other site.
Colorado United: about 11.5 mi round trip, 4,800 ft of gain from Maroon Lake; no citation, likely 14ers-derived.
Mountain Field Guide 4,800 ft; lists 14ers.com among its sources, so not independent.
List Hiker snippet: 11.7 mi RT, about 3,800 ft; listhiker is a known 14ers copier, excluded.
Trip report total including backtracking and a run up Maroon Lake Road; outing total, excluded.

evidence.fact: South Ridge standard route: 12 miles, 4,800 feet, Class 3, from Maroon Lake Trailhead.
Out/back from Maroon Lake via Crater Lake: 11.9 mi, Net Gain 5,200 ft (7.7% from 4,800).

note: Stav is Lost is independent (different figure, no citation) and within 10% of 4,800, but 11.5% from stored 4,600, so found_value wins. 14ers is the most route-precise page. No land-manager figure found. Maroon Creek Road is shuttle/reservation-only in season.

Yellowleaf 2014 Enchantments walk-through plus McClellan, 4,964 ft; traverse, not trailhead-to-summit.

trailhead: Narada Falls / Reflection Lakes (Stevens Canyon Road bend), Mount Rainier NP

figures.fact: Mountaineers page covering both Zipper and Lovers Lane together: 1,500 ft gain.
Mazamas Lane Peak, The Zipper: hike from Reflection Lakes TH, couloir to summit ridge; 2,000 ft gain (prior pass).
WillhiteWeb Lane Peak: Distance 2 miles, Elevation Gain 2,000 feet; winter start Narada Falls; author climbed the Zipper.
Sahale GPS 4.3 mi out & back, 1,980 ft; computed from map data, describes a Cliff Lake trail line, not the Zipper; excluded.

evidence.fact: Lane Peak: Distance 2 miles, Elevation Gain 2,000 feet, summit 6,012; winter approach from Narada Falls; Zipper described.
Mazamas Lane Peak, The Zipper from Reflection Lakes trailhead: 2,000 ft elevation gain.

note: WillhiteWeb is a personal guide site, independent of Mazamas, and gives 2,000 ft. Its stats are for Lane Peak in general, but the route it describes from experience is the Zipper. Mountaineers' 1,500 is 25% lower and stands alone. The two pages name different start points (Narada Falls vs Reflection Lakes) about half a mile apart on the same road. Stevens Canyon Road is closed in winter past Narada Falls.

trailhead: FR 2419 just past second Big Creek crossing (3,100 ft), Lake Cushman

figures.fact: Mountaineers: Length 8.0 mi, Elevation Gain 5,255 ft, High Point 6,255 ft; trailhead stated at 3,100 ft.
Andrew's Hikes: approach about 1 mile, 2,000 ft to the base of the route; approach only, not to summit.
Peakbagger ascent (Andrew Yi, 2021): approach gains roughly 1,600 ft to the basin below the Shield Wall; approach only.
WTA Mount Washington: 4.0 mi roundtrip, 3,190 ft gain; standard scramble route, not the Shield Wall.

note: No page gives a trailhead-to-summit gain for the Shield Wall route besides the Mountaineers 5,255. The Mountaineers' own trailhead (3,100) and high point (6,255) do not support 5,255. Also checked with no gain figure: Mountaineers TR 2021-07-31 (Hansen), CascadeClimbers TR 2009 (Off_White), Peakbagger peak pid=1048 ascents, Simmons Mountain Works (page gone). WTA's 3,190 is for the standard route (Route 1), which starts on the same road, and the stored 3,229 is within 10% of it, but it is a different route. Road washed out beyond the Mount Ellinor upper TH (2021 TR).

trailhead: Tunnel Creek Trailhead No. 1061 (3,100 ft), FR 6095 off US-2

figures.fact: Mountaineers stats: Elevation Gain 4,200 ft, high point 6,400; trip profile TH-to-pass 3,500 plus pass-to-summit 700.
The same Mountaineers page's intro: 'A pleasant 6.5 mi, 3,400 feet gain, hike along the Pacific Crest Trail'. Same publisher.
The Outbound: 13 miles out-and-back, 4,200 ft from Tunnel Creek TH. Identical to the Mountaineers figure and distance, so probably derived from it.

note: The Mountaineers page contradicts itself: the intro says 3,400 ft and the stats say 4,200 ft. Stored 3,300 is within 10% of the 3,400 intro, but that is the same publisher. The Outbound's 4,200 / 13 mi exactly mirrors Mountaineers, so independence is not shown. Also checked with no total: MP route page, Mountaineers TR 2026-09-11 (TH 3,200, Trap Pass 5,700, base 6,100), CascadeClimbers TR 2006 (Hope Lake leg only). The alternate Surprise Creek approach adds about 900 ft, according to Mountaineers.

trailhead: Barlow Pass (2,360 ft), Mountain Loop Hwy

figures.fact: Mountaineers Del Campo section: 12 miles round trip with 4,400 feet of elevation gain, from Barlow Pass via Foggy Lake.
WTA Del Campo Peak: 11.0 miles roundtrip, 4,200 ft gain, highest point 6,610, Barlow Pass trailhead.
Mountaineers headline 14 mi, 5,500 ft is Del Campo plus Gothic combined; multi-peak, excluded.

evidence.fact: Del Campo Peak: 11.0 miles roundtrip, 4,200 feet gain, highest point 6,610 feet, Barlow Pass trailhead.
Del Campo Peak (6,610 ft): 12 miles round trip with 4,400 feet of elevation gain from Barlow Pass.

note: WTA (4,200) and Mountaineers (4,400) differ, so they are independent. They agree within 4.5%. WTA states exactly the stored 4,200 on a Del Campo-only page, so I kept it; 4,400 would also pass. Neither is a land manager. The Mountain Loop Hwy is unpaved past Barlow Pass and has seasonal winter closures; WTA's page notes no closure.
